american_english: In this article, raising the primary inquiry as to how and under what conditions Vedanta philosophy has influenced Gopal Prasad Rimal's one-act play 'Maya', it is examined on the basis of established tenets of Vedanta philosophy. In Rimal's one-act play 'Maya', the injustice and oppression committed by women against women is depicted. To examine the influence of monistic Vedanta philosophy, the analysis is carried out taking Brahman as the basis. Analyzing the influence of Vedanta philosophy on the one-act play 'Maya' is the objective of this research article. This study will assist in the work of identifying philosophy within literature. In this article, Rimal's one-act play 'Maya' has been used as primary source material, and informative articles and critiques related to drama and philosophy have been utilized as secondary materials. In analyzing the facts, the deductive method has been adopted. Among the sects of Vedanta philosophy, taking the core tenets of Advaita Vedanta—such as God, soul, mind, liberation, virtue and sin, and brotherhood—as a basis, the Advaita Vedantic conclusion is drawn that if human beings treat fellow humans as humans, liberation from sorrow and troubles can be attained.
